sources.note: Builds a parallel entity grid of 27 folk-narrative motifs across 10 cultures and instruments 18 models with probing, logit lens, activation patching and generation, finding that the residual stream separates cultures cleanly in every model while the readout collapses onto Greco-Roman defaults — so the failure is at the decoder, not the encoder.
sources.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

sources.note: Applies linear probing, the logit and tuned lenses, activation patching and difference-in-means steering to two public text-to-MIDI models, and shows that the architecture of the conditioning pathway determines which steering strategy stays stable.
sources.title: MI-MIDI: Mechanistic Interpretability of Text-to-MIDI Generation Models via Probing, Lenses and Steering

sources.note: Extracts interpretable units directly from a transformer's weight matrices by column-tiled SVD, so a unit's identity is the weight rule itself rather than an atom of a separately trained dictionary, and judges them with a pre-registered suite whose central move is refusing a metric that a trivial baseline would win.
sources.title: Finding Usable Weight Mechanisms with Tiled SVD

sources.note: Refutes the standard account of vision-language hallucination -- that the model attends too little to the image -- by showing real and hallucinated objects draw equally strong attention, then uses a logit lens over the attended regions to separate two causally distinct hallucination types and treat each differently.
sources.title: Same Attention, Different Truths: Put Logit-Lens over Visual Attention to Detect and Mitigate LVLM Object Hallucination

sources.note: Treats a transformer forward pass as a controlled dynamical system with depth as time, lifts it with the Koopman operator to get a finite linear realisation whose spectrum is coordinate-free, proves that spectrum is recoverable from finite calibration data at the parametric rate, and then proves that the identifiable object and the human-legible object cannot be the same object.
sources.title: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability

sources.note: Makes trained lenses cheap enough to attach densely across a whole model — every layer, and residual, attention and MLP alike — and then uses that coverage to show that where a behaviour is most visible is not where intervening on it works best.
sources.title: Interpreting Language Model Hidden States at Scale

sources.note: Tests the claim that continuous chain-of-thought lets a model hold several candidate solutions at once, and finds it holds only for models trained from scratch: off-the-shelf models collapse a superposed input to a single token within a few layers, and fine-tuned latent reasoners solve the task in one forward pass and copy the answer through the latent slots.
sources.title: The Illusion of Superposition? A Principled Analysis of Latent Thinking in Language Models

sources.note: Activations taken just before each explicit "Step k:" marker occupy linearly separable, step-indexed regions of representation space, and how a chain moves between those regions late in the trace predicts whether the final answer will be correct, which is used to gate interventions and to steer reasoning length.
sources.title: LLM Reasoning as Trajectories: Step-Specific Representation Geometry and Correctness Signals

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

result.definition: Decoding an intermediate activation through the output unembedding to see what token it would produce, used across 8 sources as a cheap read-out of what a layer is holding. The corpus is consistent about its status: it gives a relative ordering rather than a calibrated probability, since intermediate states are not calibrated for direct decoding, and one source keeps it in raw form deliberately for cross-model comparability. That caveat has a direct methodological consequence the archive should carry -- a region or state that fails to decode may be one whose content is not yet expressed in the unembedding basis rather than one that lacks the content, so a negative logit-lens result is weak evidence. Its productive uses here are comparative rather than absolute: agreement with the sampled token rising gradually across depth in one model and jumping over three layers in another; regions attended for real objects decoding to the target token while regions attended for hallucinated ones do not; and, at scales where no full-rank reference can be trained, a trained alternative catching attacks the raw lens misses (0.80 against 0.68).
